verses.text: For the music director. For Jeduthun. A psalm by Asaph. I cry out to God! I call on him for help, asking him to hear me.
When trouble hit, I looked for the Lord. I kept my hand stretched out through the night and didn’t let it drop. My soul wouldn’t be comforted.
I think of God and groan. I voice my pain, and my spirit feels overwhelmed. Selah.
You keep my eyes wide open. I’m so upset I can’t even speak.
I think back to the old days, to years long gone.
At night I remember my song. I search my heart, and my spirit keeps asking:
“Will the Lord turn us away forever? Will he never show us favor again?
Has his faithful love disappeared for good? Has his promise failed for every generation to come?
Has God forgotten how to show grace? Has anger made him hold back his compassion?” Selah.
Then I thought, “Here’s where I’ll turn: to those years when the Most High showed the power of his right hand.”
I’ll remember what the LORD has done. I’ll remember your wonders from long ago.
I’ll think deeply about all your work and turn over in my mind what you’ve done.
God, your way is in the sanctuary. What god is as great as you?
You’re the God who works wonders. You’ve shown your strength among the peoples.
With your own arm you redeemed your people, the descendants of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
The waters saw you, God. They saw you and twisted in fear. Even the depths shook.
The clouds poured out water. Thunder rolled through the skies, and your arrows flashed all around.
Your thunder roared in the whirlwind. Lightning lit up the world, and the earth shook and trembled.
Your road ran through the sea. Your paths crossed the mighty waters, yet no one saw your footprints.
You led your people like a flock, with Moses and Aaron to guide them.
